summary: This project aims to develop a web platform called FIRE ALERT ECUADOR, designed to collect, organize, harmonize, and analyze data on hotspots and active fires provided by NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS satellite sensors. The gathered information will make it possible to identify areas with the highest concentration and frequency of forest and agricultural fires, as well as to understand their geographic distribution and behavior over time. Through interactive maps, historical calendars, statistical charts, and a dashboard, the platform will facilitate the visualization of detected hotspots, the identification of critical periods, and the generation of timely alerts regarding potential fires in Ecuador. Furthermore, it will enable the analysis of historical patterns, the recognition of unusual conditions, and the identification of areas with a high recurrence of fires, helping to pinpoint regions at potential risk. This project seeks to strengthen fire monitoring, prevention, and early response by providing organized, accessible satellite data to authorities, emergency response agencies, researchers, and local communities. In this way, it aims to support decision-making, mitigate environmental impacts, and protect biodiversity, ecosystems, and natural resources.
details:
FireGuard is a web application that transforms satellite data from NASA FIRMS into understandable territorial information regarding thermal activity in Ecuador. Its objective is to identify historical patterns of potential vegetation fires by province and canton.

The platform utilizes data from the MODIS and VIIRS S-NPP satellite sensors for the period from 2023 to 2025. It filters detections associated with potential vegetation fires and maps them to specific Ecuadorian cantons.

To avoid double-counting the same event, it groups detections occurring on the same day, within the same canton, and within an approximate 10 km grid, forming a unit referred to as a “cell-day.” It then provides:
- An interactive map of Ecuador.
- A historical calendar of monthly activity.
- A ranking of cantons with the highest activity levels.
- A historical recurrence indicator.
- A seasonal projection extending to June 2027.
- An option to download results in CSV format.
- An engaging, educational simulator.

FireGuard makes complex satellite data more accessible to students, researchers, local authorities, and the general public. It helps identify areas and time periods with heightened thermal activity, allows for the comparison of different regions, and enables the downloading of data for further analysis. It also promotes responsible interpretation by distinguishing between a satellite detection and a confirmed fire.

This project aims to serve as a useful tool for preventing fires, promoting environmental education, and improving land-use planning. For instance, if a municipality has experienced frequent fires over several years, this information could help identify the months of highest risk, allowing for proactive measures—such as organizing prevention campaigns, training local communities, and reviewing the resources available to address potential emergencies. A key contribution of this project is its use of open-source data from NASA, which it presents in a clearer, more visual, and accessible format, specifically tailored to the context of Ecuador. Furthermore, future iterations could incorporate data on climate, humidity, wind, and vegetation—alongside official reports and alert systems—to provide a more comprehensive analysis and support better decision-making regarding fire risks.


Tools, languages, and software used

Libraries and their functions within FireGuard
Pandas: Reading CSV files, filtering detections, grouping results by year, month, and canton, and calculating medians.
NumPy: Performing numerical operations, coordinate conversions, and mathematical calculations.
Shapely: Working with polygons and determining the canton in which each satellite detection is located.
FastAPI: Creating the server and routes that provide data to the map, forecast, and assistant.
Uvicorn: Running the FastAPI server so that the application can be accessed via a web browser.
Requests: Making HTTP requests to external services, such as geoBoundaries and the OpenAI API.
Programs and technologies used

FireGuard is an innovative project that aims to turn complex satellite data into clear, visual, and easy-to-understand information for people in Ecuador. Instead of simply displaying thousands of points on a map, it allows users to explore data by province and canton, see how fire activity has changed over the years, and identify areas where fires have been detected most frequently. It also includes historical calendars and maps that help highlight periods of increased fire activity. In addition, the project features an educational simulator and a QR code that make the information more accessible, especially for students and anyone interested in learning more about fires and how to prevent them.

During the development of the project, the team took into account both the reliability and limitations of satellite data. They considered that not every heat detection necessarily means that a fire has actually occurred, as well as the differences between MODIS and VIIRS satellites when collecting information. Attention was also given to the geographical location of each canton, the times of the year when more fires are recorded, and the importance of avoiding counting the same detection multiple times. In addition, the team aimed to make the platform easy to use so that anyone could understand the information without needing technical knowledge. Finally, special attention was given to clearly explaining how the data is processed and making the tool easily accessible from mobile phones.
